user.title: Connect to Tag Historian
user.description: Paste an API key with the Write scope. Create one in the Tag Historian dashboard under API keys: press Create New Key, name it, and leave Scope on Write, where the dialog opens. A Read key cannot forward anything. The key is checked against your account now; no readings are sent until you have chosen which entities to keep history for.

data_description.host: Leave this alone unless you run Tag Historian somewhere else.
data_description.api_key: The scope has to be Write. A Read key can look at your history but is refused when this integration tries to add to it.

select.title: Choose what to keep history for
select.description:
Your plan allows {tag_limit} tags. {tags_in_use} are already in use, leaving {tags_available}.

Of the {entity_count} entities enabled in this Home Assistant, the {offered_count} listed below are the ones whose job is to report something: sensors, binary sensors, numbers, number helpers and counters, less the ones Home Assistant marks as configuration and the ones whose device class makes their state a date, a time or a category name. The other {hidden_count} are things you switch, run or look up rather than things that measure. Tick "Show every entity" to list all {entity_count} instead - that list is not filtered at all.

The list is chosen by what each entity IS, not by what it happens to read at this moment, so an entity that is unavailable right now is still here.

{preselected} are ticked to start with: {breakdown}. {did_not_fit} more were worth ticking than the allowance could reach.

Nothing is sent until you finish.

data.follow_renames: Rename tags when entities are renamed
data.share_approximate_location: Use my approximate location (about 10 km) for outdoor weather from SMHI

data_description.entities: One entity costs one tag. Sensors with no device class and no state class are listed but left unticked, because Home Assistant knows nothing about them either way: most are hand-written template sensors reporting a number, but a few report a word - a house mode sitting at "away", a status sitting at "idle" - and those store nothing at all. Whatever stores nothing is counted on the "readings dropped" sensor and the entity is named there, so a series that stays empty says why. Anything you have already ticked stays in the list whatever else changes.
data_description.min_interval: Readings arriving sooner than this after the previous one for the same entity are skipped. Your daily reading allowance is spent on everything sent, so this is the setting that keeps a chatty sensor from using it up.
data_description.show_all: Puts every entity in the install in the list, unfiltered. Some of them store a 1 or a 0 - a light, a switch, a cover, an automation. The rest store nothing: a lock, a person, a climate mode and a media player all report words, and only entities whose state is a number or a plain on/off can become a reading.
data_description.follow_renames: When you rename an entity in Home Assistant, rename its tag in Tag Historian too, so its history goes on under the new name. Nothing is copied: the readings from before stay where they are and read under the new name. Off: the readings go on into the old tag, and a repair card asks whether to rename it.
data_description.share_approximate_location: Tells Tag Historian where this Home Assistant is, rounded to about 10 km before it is sent, so your charts can show the outdoor temperature and precipitation from the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute's nearest weather stations. Sweden only. It is only a proposal: a place already set in Tag Historian's Settings stays as it is, and that is where you change or remove it. Off: nothing about your location is sent.

review.title: Review
review.description:
{selected} entities selected. {new_tags} of them need a new tag, and your plan has {tags_available} free, so the whole selection fits.

At one reading every {min_interval} seconds that is at most {readings_per_day} readings a day, about {percent}% of your plan's {daily_limit}.

Nothing else to decide - submit to finish.

review_trim.title: Review - this needs more tags than you have
review_trim.description:
{selected} entities selected. {new_tags} of them need a new tag and your plan has {tags_available} free, so {overflow} do not fit.

At one reading every {min_interval} seconds that is at most {readings_per_day} readings a day, about {percent}% of your plan's {daily_limit}.

If you continue without trimming, the readings for the entities needing those {overflow} tags will be refused and lost - everything else keeps flowing.

data.trim_to_fit: Trim the selection down to what fits

data_description.trim_to_fit: Removes the lowest-ranked entities that need a new tag, and only those - an entity whose tag already exists costs nothing and is never removed to make room. Turn it off to keep your selection and accept that the extras will be refused.

history.title: Bring the history Home Assistant already has
history.description:
Home Assistant already holds history of the {selected} entities you chose, and it can come along:

- its long-term statistics: each sensor's average, minimum and maximum for every hour, or a meter's reading and use, kept for as long as Home Assistant's database lives - often years;
- what the recorder holds: every reading of the last {recorder_days} days.

Ticked, both go to Tag Historian in the background once you submit, the hourly history first. Neither counts against your daily reading allowance, and the "Tag Historian history import" sensor shows how far it is. Binary sensors, number and counter helpers, and sensors without a state_class have no long-term statistics. Their recorded readings still come.

Tag Historian is also told this Home Assistant's time zone, {time_zone}. Your account's days, months and alert times are in the account's time zone, and Tag Historian takes {time_zone} as that zone only if the account has none yet: none chosen in Tag Historian's Settings, none given to the account owner's email channel under Alarms, and none proposed earlier by a Home Assistant. It is changed in Tag Historian, under Settings.

data.import_on_setup: Bring the history Home Assistant already has

data_description.import_on_setup: The hourly history as far back as Home Assistant has it, up to ten years, then the recorder's readings. What Tag Historian already has is not stored twice. Unticked, nothing is imported now: Configure, Import the history Home Assistant already has, does it whenever you like.

reauth_confirm.title: Tag Historian needs a new API key
reauth_confirm.description: The key this integration was using is no longer accepted. Create a new one in the Tag Historian dashboard - Create New Key, with Scope set to Write - and paste it here.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that host. Check the address and that Home Assistant can get out to the internet.
error.invalid_auth: Tag Historian did not accept that key. Check you copied all of it, and that it has not been revoked.
error.read_only_key: That key's scope is Read. It can look at your data but not add to it - create a key with Scope set to Write instead.
error.account_inactive: That key belongs to an account that is not active. Sign in to the Tag Historian dashboard to see why.
error.account_blocked: Tag Historian refused the request for this account. Sign in to the dashboard to see what it needs.
error.email_not_verified: This account's email address has not been confirmed, and the grace period has passed, so Tag Historian is refusing new data. Confirm the address from the signup email and try again.
error.select_at_least_one: Pick at least one entity. An integration set up with an empty selection would sit there storing nothing and look exactly like a working one.

abort.already_configured: This Tag Historian account is already set up. Adding it twice would send every reading twice and spend your allowance twice.
abort.wrong_account: That key belongs to a different Tag Historian account. Use a key for the account this integration was set up with, or add the other account separately.
abort.reauth_successful: Tag Historian accepted the new key.
abort.no_tags_available: Your account has no free tags, and every entity you chose would need one, so trimming the selection to fit leaves nothing to historise. Nothing has been set up. Free a tag in the Tag Historian dashboard or move to a larger plan, then add this integration again.

import_history.title: Import the history Home Assistant has
import_history.description:
Sends the history Home Assistant holds for the entities below to Tag Historian, in two parts, so the history on this box is kept even if the box is not.

First its hourly long-term statistics: a measurement's average, minimum and maximum for every hour, or a meter's reading and use, as far back as Home Assistant has them and up to ten years. In Tag Historian they are hourly history, marked as Home Assistant's statistics, and they have an allowance of their own: up to ten years per tag every thirty days. Binary sensors, number and counter helpers, and sensors without a state_class have no long-term statistics.

Then what the recorder holds, with the original timestamps; the recorder here keeps {recorder_days} days of states. Imported readings do not count against your daily reading allowance. They count against your import allowance instead: {remaining} of {total} readings left - {readings_per_day} a day times your plan's {window_days}-day full-resolution window, for all imports together. Readings older than that window are skipped, and so is anything Tag Historian already has, so running an import twice stores nothing twice.

Only history is imported: readings older than the moment the import starts, older than the first reading of the entity Tag Historian received live, and older than the start of the first import of it. Everything after that is your live data, which this integration sends itself - including what is still waiting to be sent. Where a recorded reading falls in an hour the statistics brought, Tag Historian keeps the reading's hour. A renamed entity whose card you answered with "Start a new tag instead" or "Keep them apart" is left out: its history stays in the old tag.

The import runs in the background. The "Tag Historian history import" sensor shows how far it is, a notification says when it is done, and a restart carries on where it stopped.

data.statistics: Hourly history from Home Assistant's long-term statistics

data_description.entities: Only entities you keep history for are listed: an imported entity uses a tag like a forwarded one.

data_description.days: Days before today, at most ten years. Readings go back no further than your plan's full-resolution window, whatever this says.

Everything else is still being stored. Untick entities below until the selection fits, or upgrade your plan and leave it as it is.

daily_quota_exceeded.title: Tag Historian daily reading limit reached
daily_quota_exceeded.description:
Your account has used its reading allowance for today, so Tag Historian is refusing new data until the limit resets, which is {when}. Readings are held until then, through a restart too. If the wait is long the oldest are let go and read back from Home Assistant's recorder once Tag Historian takes data again, so they still arrive - and count against the next day's allowance.

Two ways out: raise the minimum interval in this integration's options so fewer readings are sent, or move to a plan with a larger allowance.

write_forbidden.description:

service_unavailable.title: Tag Historian has not been accepting data
service_unavailable.description: Writes have been failing for {minutes} minutes - Tag Historian is either unreachable or too busy to take them. Nothing about your account has changed. Readings are being held, through a restart too, and will be sent when it accepts them again; if this goes on, the oldest are let go and read back from Home Assistant's recorder afterwards. Nothing needs doing at your end.

bring_years.title: Bring the years Home Assistant already has into Tag Historian

confirm.title: Bring the years Home Assistant already has
confirm.description:
This version of the integration can bring the history Home Assistant already holds for every entity {account} keeps history for: first its hourly long-term statistics, as far back as Home Assistant has them and up to ten years, then the readings the recorder holds. In Tag Historian they become the history from before this integration was installed, marked as Home Assistant's statistics. Binary sensors, number and counter helpers, and sensors without a state_class have no long-term statistics.

Submit to start. It runs in the background - the "Tag Historian history import" sensor shows how far it is, and a notification says what it did - and it does not count against your daily reading allowance. What Tag Historian already has is not stored twice.

This integration also tells Tag Historian this Home Assistant's time zone each time it starts. Tag Historian takes it only if the account has no time zone yet: none chosen in Tag Historian's Settings, none given to the account owner's email channel under Alarms, and none proposed earlier. The account's days, months and alert times are in the account's time zone, which is changed in Tag Historian, under Settings.

Imported readings count against the account's import allowance, not the daily one, and only history is imported: nothing this integration sends live, or still has to.
